mission: Determine how much of the 2026-08-26/27 GitHub Actions disruption affected schedule-event materialization beyond the publicly stated incident windows, distinguish chronic schedule jitter from the severe S3 regime shift, and identify the strongest falsifiable explanation without claiming undocumented internals as fact.
question: Was the observable impact on GitHub Actions scheduled-trigger creation broader or longer than the public status summaries captured, and what layer best explains the JANUS 11h15m23s S3 materialization delay?

pre_s3_baseline_2026_08_17_to_26.interpretation: The schedule path was chronically late before the outage, but 2026-08-27 is a regime jump rather than ordinary continuation of the prior 27-38 minute band.

official.finding: GitHub reports write saturation on the database primary used by the service processing triggers for Actions workflows; failover did not fully recover the system; event-processing burst amplification and throttle tuning contributed; webhook queues burned down by 17:40 UTC; follow-up scalability changes were still deploying.
GitHub separately acknowledged an upstream disruption in event-processing infrastructure during the first Actions incident.

A later Actions/Pull Requests incident reported 20% of PR-triggered runs delayed over five minutes and up to 4% failing to trigger; GitHub stated full recovery beginning 23:58 UTC and resolved at 00:26 UTC Aug 27.
GitHub documents that schedule events may be delayed under high Actions load and that some queued jobs may be dropped; moving away from minute 00 is recommended.

independent_user_reports.finding: Public repo: schedule runs progressed from 39m late to 3h27m late to about 10h41m late, then later schedule fires created no run object; workflow_dispatch started within seconds.
Multiple scheduled pipelines stopped; a minimal */5 test on ubuntu-24.04 also failed to fire.

Private repo with off-hour :23 and :17 schedules: about 33 consecutive hourly schedule slots and a daily slot missed while manual workflow_dispatch succeeded; failures persisted after status returned green.

pre_incident_controls.finding: July report of schedule-triggered runs delayed 2-3h while workflow_dispatch was fast, showing schedule-specific degradation predates Aug 26.
July report of scheduled triggers stopping while workflow_dispatch continued to work, another pre-incident control against attributing the entire phenomenon to Aug 26.

timeline_bridge.observation: The JANUS scheduled event was due more than five hours after GitHub's stated full-recovery point yet materialized 11h15m23s late. Independent users reported similar schedule-only delays or missing run objects in the same post-recovery period.

competing_hypotheses.name: RESIDUAL_OR_RECURRENT_ACTIONS_TRIGGER_CONTROL_PLANE_DEGRADATION
for: manual dispatch controls in external reports
against: GitHub reported inbound queues recovered and later full recovery

competing_hypotheses.name: SCHEDULE_REGISTRATION_OR_DISPATCH_STATE_DAMAGE
for: some independent reports show no run object at all across repeated off-hour slots and successful manual dispatch
against: JANUS eventually materialized its Aug27 event rather than permanently losing it

competing_hypotheses.name: ORDINARY_DOCUMENTED_SCHEDULE_LOAD_JITTER
for: GitHub documents schedule delays under load
JANUS had chronic 18-38m delays before incident
against: multiple users report multi-hour or missing fires

competing_hypotheses.name: JANUS_REPOSITORY_LOCAL_CONFIGURATION_ERROR
against: multiple unrelated repositories show same schedule/manual split

competing_hypotheses.name: JANUS_CLOCK_OR_MEASUREMENT_BUG
against: GitHub server-side run creation timestamp supplies independent timing anchor

competing_hypotheses.name: PUBLIC_STATUS_UNDERDESCRIBED_SCHEDULE_SPECIFIC_SCOPE_OR_DURATION
for: status incident text focused on broad Actions and PR-trigger paths rather than schedule registration/materialization
against: status pages report aggregate service impact, not every sub-path; no internal schedule metrics are public

falsifiers_and_next_gates: A GitHub RCA showing schedule-event materialization was isolated from the Aug26 trigger-processing path would lower H1 same-defect confidence.
A broad matched canary set showing normal schedule materialization while JANUS alone remains delayed would raise repository-local hypotheses.
A dual-trigger control using schedule and an authorized external workflow_dispatch path on the same minimal workflow can separate schedule control-plane latency from runner/job latency.
Collect provider-independent schedule cases with server timestamps and preserve negative cases where schedules fire normally.
Watch for GitHub's promised detailed RCA or engineering follow-up and update this dossier by supersession, never by rewriting source journals.
claim_ceiling: The evidence supports a schedule-trigger/control-plane degradation class and a post-recovery observable mismatch. It does not prove GitHub's private internal mechanism, the exact causal continuity from the Aug26 incident into every Aug27 schedule failure, or intentional understatement.
